summary: Franz Boas worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Friedrich Ratzel and Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark University (~1889-1892), the Smithsonian (~1895-1896), AMNH (1896-1900), and Columbia (~1896-1942).

Franz Bopp worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Karl Windischmann (~1807-1812), Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy in Paris (~1812-1816), and at Göttingen (1820). He held posts at Humboldt University (1821-1867) and the Prussian Academy (1822-1867).

Franz Carl Christian Vorländer worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Bonn (~1824-1828) and Humboldt University (1832-1834, Ph.D.) under Franz Bopp, Karl Lachmann, and Friedrich Schleiermacher. He held posts at Humboldt University (1842) and Marburg (1843).

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz (~1953-1961, Ph.D.; PD by 1973) and at the Center for Hellenic Studies (1971-1972). He became professor at Graz in 1976.

Franz Heinrich Trithen worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Humboldt University (1838-1840) under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and Karl Lachmann, and at Oxford (1841). He held posts at Rugby School (~1844-1845), the British Museum (1844-1848), and Oxford (~1848-1851).

Franz Hessler was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Würzburg (Ph.D., 1822-1827). He served as an ordinary member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities from 1852.
Franz Josef Meier was a scholar of Indology and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1926-1931) and worked as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library from 1937 to 1970.

Franz Joseph Steingass worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. at Munich (~1843-1846) and held posts at Wakefield Grammar School and the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1889).

Franz Karl Alter worked in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. He studied at Charles University (~1770-1773), Vienna (~1774-1777), and under Paulinus of St. Bartholomew. He held posts at Vienna University Library (1779) and the University of Vienna (~1779-1804).

Indologist Franz Kielhorn studied at Göttingen, Breslau, Berlin, Leipzig (Ph.D.), and Oxford, learning under Stenzler, Weber, and Benfey. He held posts at Deccan College (1866-1881) and the University of Göttingen (1881).

Franz Misteli worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Zurich, Bonn, Geneva, and Paris. He later served as Privatdozent at Bern (1873) and as extraordinary professor (1874) and professor of comparative linguistics (1877-1898) at Basel.

Linguist Franz Nikolaus Finck studied at Munich, Paris, and Marburg (Ph.D. ~1893-1895). He held posts at Marburg (1896), Humboldt University of Berlin (PD 1903, ao. Professor 1909), and the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1903-1910).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields. He studied at Bonn (1824), Halle-Wittenberg (1824), and Humboldt University (1827-1829) under Franz Bopp. He held teaching posts at Humboldt University from 1829 and 1831.

Linguist Franz Specht studied at Humboldt University (1909-1913) and Leipzig (1909-1917, Ph.D.) under Ernst Windisch, August Leskien, Karl Brugmann, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1923-1937), Breslau (1937-1943), Humboldt University (1943-1945), and Mainz (1946-1949).

Franz Valéry Marie Cumont worked in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Charles Michel at Ghent (Ph.D. ~1884-1887), and at Bonn, Berlin, Vienna, and Paris. He held teaching posts at Ghent (1892, 1906).

Franz Woepcke worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He studied at Berlin (Ph.D. 1843-1847) and Bonn (PD ~1845-1850) under Georg Freytag, Julius Mohl, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He taught mathematics at Französisches Gymnasium Berlin (1856-1858).

Tibetologist Franz Xaver Erhard studied at Humboldt University, Free University of Berlin, Bonn, and Leipzig (Dr. phil. 2010-2015). He held posts at Humboldt University (2002-2003), Wolfson College (2016-2017), Oxford (2019), Stadtmuseum Meppen (2022), and Leipzig (2022-2023).

Franz Xaver Miklosich worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Graz (~1830-1838, Ph.D.) and Vienna (~1838-1841, Dr.iuris). He held posts at the Austrian National Library (1844-1862) and the University of Vienna (1849).

Franz von Erdmann worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Rostock (~1812-1815) and Göttingen (~1815-1817). He was Privatdozent at Rostock (1818) and professor of Oriental languages at Kazan University (~1818-1845).
Franz von László worked in Indology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1941 and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn by 1952 under doctoral supervisor Willibald Kirfel.
